[h1]Summary[/h1]
A challenging hidden object game to find 100 hidden mushrooms.

[b]Pros[/b]
+ Mushrooms
+ Challenging
+ Great music

[h1]Overview[/h1]
100 Hidden Mushrooms is a challenging hidden object game featuring 100 mushrooms of differing varieties hidden in a forest. The mushrooms come in a multitude of varieties adding to the difficulty, if you know your mushrooms you should know where and what to look for. The background art is a simple black and white drawing like many in the series but with much more lines, especially in the trees that blend and hide the mushrooms. I really enjoyed the music in this one as it sounds just like Infected Mushroom who creates Psychedelic Trance, apt for the mushroom theme I suppose.
Simple but somewhat challenging 100 hidden mushrooms.

I have ALL of the games developed by Anatoliy Loginovskikh and I have almost completed all of them. I must say, the ones I have completed so far are super AMAZING!!! The art style is as always SUPER amazing and weird. It is really easy to collect all of the hidden objects, as it is just a big one page filled with art and hidden mushrooms. The mushrooms are all different and therefore it makes it more interesting and difficult to find them all.

The only change that I would request for this game is that you cannot restart the game to play it again. When you press start again then you still see all the mushrooms you have found. On the store page it says that you can restart, however you also reset your achievements. I would recommend inserting a restart option, so that it does not reset the achievements, but only resets the mushrooms. 

For you gamers out there, I honestly feel that anyone and everyone would love this developers line of games. They are really straight forward and short games, however it is worth it.

[i]Since Steam forces a rating, choosing recommended, but this review is actually mixed. The following is mostly copied and pasted from its cookie-cutter sister titles in the series, since its artwork is the only difference.[/i]

There's not much more to add: If you like HOGs, this one's a no brainer, as it will cater to completionists with its 100 achievements. But at the same time, it's not difficult, it lacks color, and the music may wear on your nerves the longer it takes. While the price makes sense for the artwork itself, as game it is simply too short - all of the games in this series should have been combined into one. That's why if you do grab this, only buy it in a set for best value.

**100 Hidden Mushrooms** is a small but charming entry in Anatoliy Loginovskikh’s long-running series of hand-drawn hidden-object games, this time created in collaboration with artist Catherine Svyataya. Like the other titles in the developer’s catalogue, it embraces a minimalist concept and executes it with a very particular artistic identity. The premise is simple enough—you are presented with a large, detailed illustration and must locate one hundred mushrooms cleverly tucked throughout the scene—but the charm lies in how the visual presentation and gentle pacing turn that simplicity into a relaxing, almost meditative experience.

The artwork is easily the game’s standout element. Rendered entirely in black and white, the forest scene is dense with whimsical lines, stylized shapes, and fairytale motifs. Svyataya’s illustrations give the environment a surreal, storybook quality, filled with expressive characters, tiny decorative flourishes, and unexpected details that encourage the player to slow down and scan every nook with intention. The absence of color works in the game’s favor: it removes visual noise and lets the mushrooms blend into the landscape in subtle ways. Instead of relying on bright highlights to guide the eye, the game encourages players to pay attention to form, outline, shadow, and negative space. This makes the search feel like a true visual puzzle rather than a quick click-fest.

Mechanically, the game is stripped down to its core function. You click on mushrooms, increase your found count, and progress at your own pace. There are no timers, penalties, hint systems, or layered objectives. For many players this is precisely the appeal—there is nothing to distract from the slow, satisfying process of combing through the image. The lack of traditional puzzle elements or mechanical depth might disappoint players who expect variety or escalating challenge, but for those who know what they are getting into, the purity of the experience is refreshing. The absence of zoom functionality can occasionally make some smaller mushrooms trickier to spot, though the overall design seems tuned to keep frustration low. It is a game that embraces patience rather than pressure.

Because of its simplicity, **100 Hidden Mushrooms** is undeniably short. Many players will complete it in a matter of minutes rather than hours, depending on how meticulous they are. Its replay value comes mainly from achievement hunting or the desire to revisit the artwork rather than from procedural content or multiple levels. This brevity is part of its identity, and given its low price point, the compact runtime feels appropriate. It is a small experience meant to be consumed in a single sitting, like a miniature puzzle book or a quick artistic vignette between larger games.

At its core, the game succeeds because it understands its audience. It does not attempt to broaden its scope beyond what it promises. The hand-drawn forest scene is cozy, imaginative, and relaxing to explore, and locating each mushroom feels like participating in an artist’s playful challenge. The title fits comfortably into the niche the developer has carved out over years: simple, inexpensive hidden-object games with a distinctive monochrome art style and a gentle tone. Those seeking depth, challenge, or variety will find little here, but those who appreciate quiet artistic puzzles will find the experience delightful despite (or even because of) its modest size.

Taken as a whole, **100 Hidden Mushrooms** offers a brief but pleasant escape—an invitation to step into a whimsical sketch and enjoy the process of discovery. It is not a game built on complexity, but one built on atmosphere and simplicity, and for players who value that kind of focused experience, it delivers exactly what it sets out to provide.

[h1][b]Like its siblings: short, loud, unimaginative[/b][/h1]

[h3][b]What this game is:[/b][/h3] A hidden mushroom game, like other hidden animals/items theme games found on Steam. This one is short, easy and not very elaborate, like many others by Anatoliy Loginovskikh. 

[h3][b]How does it work?[/b][/h3] It is a basic point and click game. You have to find all the hidden mushrooms in a B&W picture.  You go progressively down the only picture and click on all the mushrooms you can find to turn them red. 

[h3][b]How does it perform?[/b][/h3] Very easy to play. You click on each mushroom you find and its colour changes to red. Going quickly, you will find all mushrooms in a matter of less than half an hour. 

[h3][b]The good points:[/b][/h3] Simple and easy game. You only need to sit and click. Getting the Achievements is very easy. There are no apparent bugs. Takes less than 10 MB on your HD, and will run on a 10 years old PC.  You can expect 20 to 30 minutes (if you plays slowly) of entertainement out of it. There are Steam Trading Cards and easy Achievements.  It can be played on the Steam Deck.

[h3][b]The bad points:[/b][/h3] The game is short and the replay value is extremely limited. The music is ok but loud, and it is impossible to shut it down or lower the volume.  The whole thing is unimaginative. They could have at least added a timer mode in order to provide some more challenge, and some replay value.  What you see is what you get. There is no menu to speak of, and no settings you can tweak in order to make your gaming experience better and more enjoyable. 

[h3][b]My take on this:[/b][/h3] As it is, this game is just a rehash of similarly priced cats games but worse.  It is too short, too easy, has no controls to speak of, and appears to be some sort of easy do, rince and repeat scheme in order to make money.  As it is, I won't recommend it.  There are equivalent free games on Steam that are way more entertaining than this one, and are better made.  Buy only IF it is for sale and you want the easy Achievements and Steam Trade Cards.
